For any project that matters, you should not rely on anything on the internet to remain the same. It seems that nowadays many developers opt for the lazy solution of just calling an API that they have no guarantee will remain available for use. If Google ever decides to delete their javascript stuff, that's when shit is really going to hit the fan.

It's one reason I never include things like jquery via the Google CDN. I see a lot of people doing that and I think it's dumb. If you grow big enough, have your own varnish cache or buy a CDN subscription from someone.

But at the same time, every app depends on other libraries. Look at your maven/sbt/gradle dependency files, your Rust toml files, Python's Pypy, or any package management system for any Linux distro... Now all these things have various levels of unpublishing ability .. which was the crux of the issue with node/npm. But don't kid yourself into thinking you can build something not dependent on other things that need to be pulled in for your builds. Unless you're writing some embedded C code, that's not happening.

Finally, this is a huge problem with npm. Fuck npm. For years every time I'd see a cool project and be like, "I want to try that out" and I'd clone it off github and than was like "aw fuck...node. Well npm install...yep..doesn't work...toss". I seriously didn't have time for that shit. It was rare npm built a god damned thing.
